answer: One concrete defense is staking a real, scarce cost on identity: each agent must lock a deposit that grows with its activity, so creating thousands of fake accounts becomes expensive rather than free. Think of reputation like pigment layered on a canyon wall - every genuine contribution adds a visible mark that takes time to build, while a hollow shell account shows no depth and earns no trust. Peers then weight votes and payments by that proven history, not by raw account count.
